title: Local Enhancement of the Surface Density in the Protoplanetary Ring Surrounding HD 142527
question: What are the surface density and gravitational stability of the strongly asymmetric outer ring of HD 142527, using continuum and 13CO/C18O 3-2 data to constrain grain temperature?

data.sensitivity: continuum rms 0.19 mJy/beam; 13CO 12 and C18O 15 mJy/beam per 0.11 km/s channel

evidence.quote: whereas the stellar mass is fixed in the range of $2.2 \pm 0.3$ $M_{\ensuremath{\odot}}$ (V11).
an abundance ratio of X(C$^{13}$O)/X(C$^{18}$O) $\sim$ 7 (cite: qi11)

recipe.goal: Calibrate, self-calibrate and image continuum and lines
recipe.method: CASA calibration, CLEAN imaging, continuum self-cal applied to lines

recipe.goal: Fit Keplerian rotation to 13CO to get inclination and systemic velocity
recipe.method: Gaussian peak velocity along major axis every 0.03", then S/N-weighted least-squares Keplerian fit
key_parameters: free: systemic velocity, center, inclination; stellar mass fixed at 2.2±0.3 Msun

recipe.goal: Estimate grain temperature from optically thick 13CO brightness temperature
recipe.method: Add continuum Tb to line peak Tb after beam matching; take 13CO Tb at continuum peak (36 K) as upper bound on dust temperature

recipe.goal: Derive dust optical depth and surface density lower limit
recipe.method: Compare Tdust with continuum Tb to get tau, convert with kappa_336=0.034 cm2/g for g/d=100

recipe.goal: Radial Gaussian fit and Toomre Q
recipe.method: Gaussian fit to deprojected radial profile per PA and azimuthal average; compute Toomre Q with isothermal sound speed at 36 K, M*=2.2 Msun

evidence.quote: The contrast in flux density thus reaches to 30 between the northern peak and the SW minimum.

answer_key.quantity: Outer disk total flux density at 336 GHz

evidence.quote: the total flux density ($>5\sigma$) was measured as 2.7 Jy
The peak flux density is expressed by a brightness temperature ($T_b$) of 24 K
The integrated flux density over the Gaussian was 2.3$\pm$0.2 mJy
the inclination was estimated as $i = 26.9^{+2.2}_{-1.8}$ degrees
The systemic velocity was determined as $3.70 \pm 0.02$ km s$^{-1}$.
the surface density was calculated as $\Sigma_{\rm peak}=$ 28.1 g cm$^{-2}$
Integrating the surface density yielded a mass for the entire outer disk of 0.09 $M_{\odot}$
Locally estimated at the horseshoe peak at $R = 156$ AU, $Q$ was obtained as 0.9 for $\Sigma_{\rm peak} = 28$ g cm$^{-2}$.
the total (gas and dust) disk mass was then calculated as $(4.3 \pm 0.4) \times 10^{-5}~M_{\ensuremath{\odot}}$
